title: Good Measure, Running Over
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: God did not measure out his mercy in small portions. He gave us his Son, and he calls us to give with the same open hand.
exhortation: Have you ever had to share with a stingy person? It's not very fun, right? Everyone is a little anxious, worried about whether they're going to get enough. Everybody's grasping. On the other hand, being with a generous person is usually a lot of fun. It's life-giving. Why? Because a generous person is thinking about others, not about what they can get or what they have.

That's how God is with us, and that is how God wants us to be with others. He is saying, "Don't worry about what you've got. I have plenty more where that came from. Focus on being generous toward others, and you're going to be just fine." More than fine. You will be blessed.

So what changes how we hear this verse at Thanksgiving? Remembering that the Father did not measure out his mercy to us carefully, in small, miserly portions. No, he gave us his Son. At the cross, the measure of love and mercy and grace spilled over in generous amounts.

This verse has been sold as a kind of scheme: send your gift in, get this return. Like a transaction. But read what surrounds the verse. Love your enemies. Lend, expecting nothing back. Judge not. Forgive.

Our culture looks for prosperity in a grasping, tight-fisted way. Go get everything you can and hang on to it for dear life. Save it all so you can have a big, beautiful house and never worry about anything, all by hoarding and keeping it for yourself. Scripture points us toward something very different: an open hand. Jesus is not teaching us a new method to corner God into giving us what we want. He's showing us the heart of the Father, what God is like, and he's calling us to resemble him.

Charles Spurgeon saw this principle in the human body. The heart doesn't take in blood to store it. What comes in through one valve goes out through another, and any part of the body that started to hoard would become diseased. The whole body lives by giving. The same is true of the soul. Blessing that stops with us goes stagnant.

So here's the question for this Thanksgiving: what measure are you using, God's or the world's? Some of you will sit across from someone this week who has hurt you. The verse right before this one says, "Forgive." Bring a bigger measure to that table. Some of you know someone who will eat alone. Pull up a chair. Some of you have been holding tightly to what God gave you because you're afraid there won't be enough. Open your hand.

Jesus doesn't promise you a bigger bank account. He promises you a Father who cannot be outgiven, who will settle every account in his own time with his own generous hand. So give thanks, and then give. Press it down, shake it together, let it run over, just as God has done for us through Jesus. Thanks be to God for his inexpressible gift.
